scoring.globalScore: average of all applicable rules across every criterion, 0-100

dimensions.name: Prompting
dimensions.summary: Check that the system informs and guides the user throughout the interaction.

rules.text: Are the titles of screens, windows and dialog boxes placed at the top, centered or left-justified?
Do all fields and data displays have identifying labels?
If the data to be entered has a particular format, is that format described on the screen?
Are the units for entering or displaying metric or financial data described on the screen?
Do field labels contain a specific element (e.g. ':') as an invitation for data entry?
If the data to be entered has acceptable values, are those values described on the screen?
Do long lists show indicators of continuation, item count and pages?
Do tables present row and column headers that are consistent and distinguishable from the displayed data?
Do charts have an overall title and labels for their axes?
Do buttons that open dialog boxes show the '…' sign in their labels as an indicator of dialog continuity?
Do menu pages have titles, headers or entry prompts?
Do menu options that lead to other menu panels show the '>' sign to indicate that?
Does the user find the information needed for their actions readily available?
In error message boxes, is a 'HELP' command button always present?
Is the response to a user's help request structured within the context of the current task and transaction?
Is it possible for the user to obtain the list of the basic commands of the language?
When errors occur, can the user access all the information needed to diagnose and solve the problem?

dimensions.name: Grouping by Location
dimensions.summary: Check that the spatial distribution of items reflects the relationships between the information.

rules.text: Is the presentation space laid out in small functional zones?
Does the arrangement of the interaction objects in a dialog box follow a logical order?
In data groupings, are items organized spatially according to a logical criterion?
Are the accelerator-key codes of menu options located to the right of the option name?
In selection lists, are the options organized according to some logical order?
Are menu panels built from a logical criterion for grouping options?
Within a menu panel, are mutually exclusive or interdependent options grouped together and separated from the others?
Are the options within a menu panel ordered according to some logical criterion?
Does the definition of the menu option selected by default follow some criterion?
Are groups of command buttons placed in a column to the right, or in a row below the objects they are associated with?
Is the command button selected by default in the topmost position (vertical buttons) or leftmost position (horizontal buttons)?

dimensions.name: Grouping by Format
dimensions.summary: Check the visual format of items as a means of conveying associations and differences.

rules.text: Are controls and commands visually differentiated from the information presented on the screens?
Are visual codes used to associate different categories of data that are dispersed across the screens?
Are the different types of elements on a query screen (data, commands and instructions) visually distinct from one another?
Are labels visually different from the data they are associated with?
Are table headers differentiated through the use of different colors, larger letters or underlining?
In abnormal situations, are critical data requiring immediate attention differentiated through bright colors such as red or pink?
Are sound signals used to alert users in relation to a visual presentation?
In text presentation, are style resources (italic, bold, underline, different fonts) used to highlight important words or notions?
Are items selected for change, update or activation highlighted from the others?
In alarm situations and high information-density screens, is visual blinking used to highlight data and information?
Are required fields differentiated from optional fields in a visually clear way?
In message boxes, does the default-selected button have a visual presentation sufficiently distinct from the others?
In situations requiring special attention, are alert and warning messages presented in a distinct way?
Is the mouse cursor shape different from any other item presented?
Are the shapes of cursors presented simultaneously sufficiently distinct from one another?
Are grouping boxes used to emphasize a group of related data?
When presenting options that are currently unavailable, does the system show them in a visually differentiated way?

dimensions.name: Feedback
dimensions.summary: Assess the quality of the immediate feedback to the user's actions.

rules.text: Does the system provide feedback for all of the user's actions?
When the system becomes unavailable due to long processing, is the user warned of this state and of the duration of the unavailability?
Does the system provide information about the status of print jobs?
Are items selected from a list visually highlighted immediately?
Does the cursor image provide dynamic and contextual feedback about direct manipulation?
Does the system give the user information about the duration of lengthy processing?
Does the system present a message informing about the success or failure of lengthy processing?
Does the system provide immediate and continuous feedback for direct manipulations?
Does the system set the action focus to newly created or newly opened objects?
Does the system provide feedback about changes to the attributes of objects?
Is any change in the current state of control objects presented visually and clearly to the user?
Does the system provide a history of the commands entered by the user during a work session?

dimensions.name: Legibility
dimensions.summary: Check the legibility of the information presented on the system's screens.

rules.text: Is blank space used to separate logical groups rather than placing everything on one side of the screen?
In dialog boxes and composite objects, are control and presentation objects aligned vertically and horizontally?
Are vertically organized field labels of varying sizes right-justified?
Is the minimum width of displayed text 50 characters?
Is the minimum height of text display areas 4 lines?
Are text paragraphs separated by at least one blank line?
Is the exclusive use of uppercase letters in text avoided?
Is the use of bold minimized?
Is the use of underline minimized?
Are blank lines used to separate groups in tables?
Are alphabetically organized data lists left-justified?
Are lists with decimal numbers aligned by the decimal point?
Are the lines for framing and segmenting menus simple?
Are menu panel borders separated enough from the option text to preserve legibility?
Is the use of abbreviations in menus minimized?
Do menu option names have only the initial letter capitalized?
Are menu option numbers right-aligned?
If alphabetical enumeration is used, are the selection letters left-aligned?
Are the options of a horizontal menu bar separated by at least 2 spaces?
Do field labels begin with a capital letter and continue in lowercase?
Are long data items partitioned into smaller groups in entries and displays?
Do the system's alphanumeric codes group letters and numbers separately?
Are icons legible?
Does the system use text labels when there is icon ambiguity?
Is reverse-video information always legible?
Is the use of reverse video restricted to indicating selection feedback?
Is the presented data continuous rather than blinking?

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.summary: Check the length of the codes and terms presented and entered into the system.

rules.text: Does the system offer default values to speed up data entry?
Is the alphanumeric identification of windows short enough to be easily remembered?
Are menu option names concise?
Are icons economical in terms of screen space?
Are the denominations brief?
Are abbreviations short?
Are arbitrary codes that the user must memorize always shorter than 4 or 5 characters?
Are labels concise?
Are non-meaningful alphanumeric codes that must be entered shorter than 7 characters?
When entering alphanumeric data, does the system treat uppercase and lowercase letters as equivalent?
When entering numeric data, is the user freed from filling in unnecessary decimal points?
When entering numeric data, is the user freed from filling in unnecessary trailing fractional zeros?
When entering metric or financial values, is the user freed from filling in the unit of measure?
Is the user allowed to reuse values defined for previous entries, and even to modify them?

dimensions.name: Minimal Actions
dimensions.summary: Check the length of the dialogs required to accomplish the user's goals.

rules.text: In data-entry forms, does the system position the cursor at the start of the first input field?
When performing the main actions of a dialog box, are cursor movements minimized through proper ordering of the objects?
Does the user have a simple and quick way (e.g. the TAB key) to navigate between the fields of a form?
Do command-button groups always have one button defined as the default?
Is the menu structure designed to reduce the steps needed for selection?

dimensions.name: Information Density
dimensions.summary: Assess the information density of the screens presented by the system.

rules.text: Is the information density of the windows reduced?
Do the screens present only the data and information that are necessary and indispensable to the user for their task?
When entering coded data, are only the necessary data present on the screen in a distinguishable way?
Does the system minimize the need for the user to remember exact data from one screen to another?
When reading a window, are the user's eye movements minimized by distributing the main objects along the lines of a 'Z'?
Does the system avoid presenting a large number of windows that may distract or overload the user's memory?
When manipulating the presented data, is the user freed from translating units?
Do selection and combo lists present a height corresponding to at most nine lines?
Do menu panels show as active only the necessary options?

dimensions.name: Explicit User Actions
dimensions.summary: Check that it is the user who explicitly commands the system's actions.

rules.text: Does the system defer processing until the user's input actions have been completed?
During the selection of a menu option, does the system allow separation between indicating and executing the option?
To start processing the data, does the system always require an explicit 'ENTER' action from the user?
Is it always the user who commands navigation between the fields of a form?

dimensions.name: User Control
dimensions.summary: Assess the user's ability to control the sequencing and execution of actions.

rules.text: Can the user end a repetitive sequential dialog at any moment?
Can the user interrupt and resume a sequential dialog at any moment?
Can the user restart a sequential dialog at any moment?
During periods when input devices are blocked, does the system provide an option to interrupt the process that caused the block?

dimensions.name: Flexibility
dimensions.summary: Assess the system's options for personalization by the user.

rules.text: Does the system let the user personalize actions to account for their needs, habits or preferences?

dimensions.name: User Experience
dimensions.summary: Assess the opportunities for success of users with different levels of experience.

rules.text: Does the system offer opportunities for success to both novice and experienced users (e.g. shortcuts, assistance)?

dimensions.name: Error Protection
dimensions.summary: Assess the mechanisms used to prevent user errors.

rules.text: Does the system have mechanisms that prevent user errors before they occur?

dimensions.name: Error Messages
dimensions.summary: Assess the quality of the error messages presented to users.

rules.text: Are error messages clear and precise, indicating the cause of the error and how to correct it?

dimensions.name: Error Correction
dimensions.summary: Assess the facilities offered to the user for correcting the errors they make.

rules.text: Does the system offer easy means for the user to correct the errors they make (e.g. undo, redo, editing)?

dimensions.name: Consistency
dimensions.summary: Assess the coherence of the interface's design elements.

rules.text: Are design choices (codes, denominations, formats, procedures) kept identical in identical contexts and different in different contexts?

dimensions.name: Significance of Codes
dimensions.summary: Assess the clarity of the codes and denominations used by the interface.

rules.text: Are codes, denominations, abbreviations and terms meaningful and familiar to the user, with a strong relationship to their referent?

dimensions.name: Compatibility
dimensions.summary: Assess the alignment of the system with the user's expectations, characteristics and task.

rules.text: Is the system compatible with the user's characteristics (memory, perception, habits) and with their task and environment?
